Exploratory learning retry · 28 October 2026 · one seed

Official FlashSAC cable retry

Pristine authors’ compiled Torch FP16 AMP learner in the stock Isaac cable task, with three-step returns and a longer learning-rate schedule.

Study question. What happens in one fresh seed 2 run after changing n1→n3 and the shared per-optimizer decay horizon 12,800→96,000 together? Each run collects 49,152,000 transitions; nine checkpoints use the same 128 physical evaluation states. The historical reference is separately audited. This bundle does not isolate either change or establish reliable learning.

Observed outcome. Neither the historical run nor this retry demonstrated cable pickup under the common evaluation. All nine saved checkpoints in each run recorded 0% goal attainment, final hold and lift. The higher evaluation return in the retry does not establish pickup.

Ever goal means segment 6 came strictly within 5 cm of its commanded XYZ. Occupancy uses the full 128×150 episode-step budget. Final hold requires the last 15 steps within goal; lift separately means middle-segment height exceeded 5 cm. These geometry metrics do not confirm contact or grasp. No population task-solved threshold is introduced.

Physical evaluation and stochastic training

All evaluations use full cable gravity −9.81 m/s² and final action-rate penalty −0.1, including checkpoint 0. Training retains stock gravity and action-rate curricula. Collection geometry includes warmup and autoreset episodes; its world-ever fractions are not per-episode evaluation success. The historical run lacks these new stochastic geometry fields.

Update, action and reward evidence

Alpha is an entropy loss coefficient rather than a direct action-noise multiplier. Negative differential entropy is valid. The 8-action Gaussian-reference sigma 0.15 gives target −3.82545 nats, not a measured rollout standard deviation. Historical discounted-return moments and maximum reward magnitude determine adaptive reward scaling; interaction with curricula is a hypothesis, not an established cause. Critic support saturation is not established by the logged losses.

Observed execution costs

The historical official worker ran fourth in a four-recipe allocation, whereas this pilot follows one selected official smoke. GPU, chronology, shared compiler caches, trajectories and diagnostic cost can differ. Full process wall includes final replay export; parent training/evaluation clocks are shown separately from nested loop/startup components. Host collection/learning scopes are not isolated GPU kernel latency.

Recipe and continuation limits

Architecture, losses, 10M replay, 100,000 warmup, batch 2048, gamma 0.99, peak 3e-4 and floor 1.5e-4 are retained. Each optimizer advances its own pristine scheduler on attempted updates, including AMP skips, against the same 96,000 horizon. Actor/temperature update half as often and therefore do not reach the critic’s final LR. The public n3 replay export omits two pending vector batches, global RNG and simulator state; it does not promise exact collector trajectory continuation. No native 3-step parity is asserted.
